pages.title: The Weight of a Fraction
pages.text:
SCHEMIN ’26 | WEEK 6 RECAP | FOLIO 02
OPENING DRIVE
THE WEIGHT OF A FRACTION
Six contests. Two extraordinary escapes. A Commonwealth forced to reckon.

In most weeks, winning is easy to recognize. Someone towers over a scoreboard, someone falls out of the frame, and the Commonwealth collects the debris by sunrise. Week Six did not offer that kindness.

At the swamp, His Majesty’s Blood survived Mud Dogs by twelve hundredths of a point, the difference between a deed waved in triumph and a deed dragged back into the muck. At the falls, Three Dreaded Snake edged The LLC by thirty-seven hundredths, a margin too narrow to bridge the distance between a promise and an actual bargain. Elsewhere, Slob on my Dobb did not bother with subtlety. The week’s largest score—143.70—sent ObiWan Jacoby home from the dodgeball court with questions for the officials, and possibly for the scoreboard operator.

D0nkey K0ng invaded the Theatre of Ruins and stole the football afternoon. Duckhook held the clubhouse against El Niño. Seven Deadly Chins rode out with the final word in the Chili Stable. Six contests; six winners; not a single permission slip for the league to relax.

pages.title: Theatre of Ruins — Visitors at the Gates
pages.text:
SCHEMIN ’26
FANTASY FOOTBALL MEMO
WEEK 6 | Folio 04
THEATRE OF RUINS
Visitors at the Gates
Red Leopards (HOME) vs D0nkey K0ng (AWAY)
Red Leopard Ruins, Storm Coast
SAME GAME OLDER WARS
RED LEOPARDS
6

Rain threaded the terraces of the Red Leopard Ruins before the visiting supporters could be heard. When they came, it was with a chorus of Arsenal-colored banners, rolling up the escarpment like a second front. The Red Leopards had built an afternoon around rivalry: Manchester United colors, a football field drawn into the ruin’s available floor, and a tunnel entrance grand enough to make a lion of any ordinary arrival.

The visitor was not ordinary. D0nkey K0ng stepped into view as one vast integrated figure: gorilla above, four equine legs below, a single body carrying its own momentum. A scarf swung from one shoulder. Every attempt at a gracious arrival became a minor argument with a stairway.

The Leopard’s tail lashed beneath his kit. “You brought a cavalry unit to a football match?”
DK looked down at the field. “You built me four lanes.”

The crowd divided the rain with noise. For a moment the ancient ruins seemed to remember they were supposed to be a fortress. Then the whistle blew, and the fortress discovered it was hosting a derby.

“You brought a cavalry unit to a football match?”
— RED LEOPARD
“You built me four lanes.”
— DONKEY KONG

THEATRE OF RUINS
Four Lanes to Victory
Red Leopards (HOME) vs D0nkey K0ng (AWAY)
Red Leopard Ruins, Storm Coast
SAME GAME OLDER WARS
RED LEOPARDS
6

“The visiting end answered with another song.”

FINAL: D0nkey K0ng 118.96 — Red Leopards 108.08

The Leopard played as if the home terraces could close the distance for him. He cut across broken light, darted between challenges, and chased the kind of curling finish that makes an afternoon survive decades. DK answered with the stubborn geometry of four legs: no easy human footwork, no mistaken mascot pose, just one towering integrated body learning to turn momentum into angles.

Behind the terraces, supporters argued over which famous football memory the ruins were imitating. On the field, the rivalry made its own. The home crowd howled for an equalizer. The visiting end answered with another song, louder each time the ball reached the open lane.

When the final whistle arrived, the fortress had a new result to remember: D0nkey K0ng 118.96, Red Leopards 108.08. The stairs had welcomed a visitor; the pitch had failed to dismiss him.

FINAL: D0nkey K0ng 118.96 — Red Leopards 108.08

DK’s supporters were suddenly much louder than the weather. The Leopard stood near the painted touchline, refusing to look at anyone holding a red scarf. DK offered a gesture somewhere between respect and provocation.

THE COUNTRY CLUB OF JACKSON.
PRISTINE COURSE. QUESTIONABLE WEATHER.
PART I — THE FORECAST DOES NOT CONCERN THE CLUB

The Country Club of Jackson had survived questionable members, misplaced scorecards, and one unfortunate debate over whether a golf cart counted as formal transportation. Weather, however, was considered a problem for less reputable establishments.

Dr. Duckhook arrived at the first tee immaculate. His cap sat perfectly. His gloves were clean. His caddie had polished the clubs so thorughly that the approaching thunderhead appeared in the reflection.

Across the fairway, the sky turned the color of a membership application rejected on principle.

J

pages.title: The Jackson Invitational — The Clubhouse Refuses to Notice
pages.text:
SCHEMIN’ 26 | WEEK 6 | FOLIO 08
THE JACKSON INVITATIONAL
THE COUNTRY CLUB OF JACKSON.
PRISTINE COURSE. QUESTIONABLE WEATHER.
PART II — THE CLUBHOUSE REFUSES TO NOTICE

By the eighteenth hole, the Country Club of Jackson had developed several new water hazards, none of which appeared on the architect’s original plans.
The head groundskeeper had installed a pump beside the bunker. It removed water with impressive efficiency, provided nobody asked where the water went afterward.
Unfortunately, the discharge hose was pointed at the tournament committee.
A caddie disappeared beneath an overturned umbrella. Two members argued over whether standing water qualified as a temporary obstruction or an unauthorized swimming facility.
Through it all, Dr. Duckhook continued playing.
The storm bent the flags, flooded the bunkers, and reduced the clubhouse’s carefully maintained dignity to a collection of damp napkins.
It did not stop Duckhook.
His final putt rolled across the soaked green and dropped into the cup.
The groundskeeper’s pump chose that precise moment to erupt into a fountain.
The committee received the full force of its engineering achievement.
Duckhook accepted the applause as though nothing unusual had happened.
“Remarkable conditions,” the club secretary said.
“Quite,” Duckhook replied. “The course practically watered itself.”
The final fantasy ledger recorded Dr. Duckhook 132.40, El Niño 119.86.
The weather had arrived.
The winner had never left.

RULES OF GOLF
J

SLOB’S FOOTHILL CAMP
SAME COURT. SAME RULES. DIFFERENT RESULTS.
THE RIGGED COURT

The dodgeball court at Foothill Camp had three truths. The centerline was straight. The judge’s platform had an unobstructed view. And somehow every controversial call seemed to favor whoever knew the referee’s cousin.

ObiWan Jacoby crossed into Slob’s camp with the calm of a traveler who had seen elaborate scams and survived them. Slob stood beside the officials’ stand explaining, with great seriousness, why the rules had needed a “local adjustment.” A whistle sounded before either contestant had moved.

“Out,” said the judge.
“Who?” ObiWan asked.
“Pending review,” said Slob.

pages.title: The Blackwater Deed Job — Part I — The Bargain
pages.text:
SCHEMIN’ 26 | WEEK 6
FOLIO 13
The BLACKWATER DEED JOB
PART I — THE BARGAIN
MUD DOGS (HOME)
VS
HIS MAJESTY’S BLOOD (AWAY)
MUD SWAMP.
SAME LAND. DIFFERENT LAWS.

The Mud Dogs had arranged a meeting where the river made promises hard to enforce: a low barge, a chest of damp papers, and marsh banks that looked identical from every angle. His Majesty’s Blood arrived hooded and armored, the red eyes of his approved form holding a steady place within the dark. The Belt remained his, independent of the week’s fantasy result.

Mud spread a wrinkled diagram over a crate. It claimed to show a piece of the swamp worth more than any reasonable creature should wish to own.

“You’ve asked me here to sign a map,” Blood said.
“A map,” Mud replied, “is a deed that hasn’t learned confidence.”

The channel offered no opinion. It did, however, move the barge an inconvenient distance while both parties leaned over the ink. A latch snapped shut on the chest. The papers were suddenly more important than the people holding them.

BLACKWATER SWAMP

pages.title: The Blackwater Deed Job — Part II — The 0.12 Escape
pages.text:
SCHEMIN’ 26 | WEEK 6
FOLIO 14
The BLACKWATER DEED JOB
PART II — THE 0.12 ESCAPE
MUD DOGS (HOME)
VS
HIS MAJESTY’S BLOOD (AWAY)
MUD SWAMP.
SAME LAND. DIFFERENT LAWS.

The account would later be simplified into a contest for ownership. That was never settled. The barge was a temporary office, the chest held documents of unverified force, and neither participant had produced a lawful land transfer recognized by the Commonwealth.

What was settled was a football result: His Majesty’s Blood 136.92, Mud Dogs 136.80. Twelve hundredths. A margin so narrow Mud tried to make the number stand still by writing it twice.

Blood did not celebrate extravagantly. He simply closed the lid of the chest, watched the barge rotate in the slow current, and took his leave with the Belt exactly where it belonged.

“You didn’t even buy anything.”
MUD DOGS
“No. But I won.”
HIS MAJESTY’S BLOOD

The river carried the words downstream. The paperwork remained what it had been at the start: suspicious, unsigned in any authoritative sense, and dramatically inconvenient.

BLACKWATER SWAMP
FINAL — WEEK 6
HIS MAJESTY’S BLOOD 136.92 WINNER
MUD DOGS 136.80 DEFEATED
VICTORY MARGIN: 0.12 POINTS

The FALLS PROTOCOL
PART I — THE PROPOSAL
THREE DREADED SNAKE (HOME)
VS
THE LLC (AWAY)
WATERFALL TEMPLE.
SAME FALLS. DIFFERENT TERMS.

Mist covered the Waterfall Temple stairs so completely that The LLC could hear Three Dreaded Snake before seeing him. Three heads appeared above one coiled body, each considering a different aspect of the negotiation. One asked about cost. One asked about liability. The third wanted to know why the visitor had brought so many papers to a place made mostly of water.

The LLC unfolded a plan across a stone ledge. It contained a crossing, possible future access, and a quantity of fine print that the waterfall attempted to erase.

“This is a framework,” LLC explained.

FIRST HEAD (ON COST)
“Then where is the frame?”
SECOND HEAD (ON LIABILITY)
“Where is the bridge?”
THIRD HEAD (ON ACCESS)
“Where is the exit?”

LLC
CROSSING PLAN
ACCESS OPTIONS
RISK & LIABILITY

Their arguments were interrupted by a gust that lifted a corner of the plan over the spray. Neither a bridge nor a vault was built. The conversation was a negotiation, not a binding contract.

pages.title: The Falls Protocol — Part II — The Fine Print
pages.text:
SCHEMIN’ 26 | WEEK 6
FOLIO 16
The FALLS PROTOCOL
PART II — THE FINE PRINT

For all the paper placed between them, the two parties were finally divided by something very small: Three Dreaded Snake scored 138.06 to The LLC’s 137.69, a victory of thirty-seven hundredths.

The first head named it a decisive triumph. The second called it a statistical inconvenience. The third announced that anyone hoping to cross the waterfall would still need to use the actual stairs.

The LLC gathered his forms and looked toward the mist. “We can revisit the deal.”
“We can,” said one head.
“We might,” said another.
“We won’t do it today,” concluded the third.

The pages left dry enough to be filed and damp enough to be doubted. The temple was unchanged. Its keeper had won. The proposed crossing remained a proposal.

THE HIGHLANDS ARE CROWDED
Two powers sit at 4–2, and neither can claim the summit outright. ObiWan Jacoby holds ESPN’s top playoff seed; D0nkey K0ng boasts 881.03 points and a victory inside Red Leopard Ruins. Three Dreaded Snake has clawed back to 3–3, while Mud Dogs sits 2–4 after losing by twelve hundredths. The highlands look orderly from a distance. The records say otherwise.

FOUR TEAMS. ONE RECORD.
Red Leopards. Slob on my Dobb. The Chili Cheesers. Dr. Duckhook. All 3–3. Not one game separates them in the standings. Slob’s 940.86 points lead the league, Chili has scored 879.82, and Duckhook comes off a storm-soaked win. Red’s next visitor is His Majesty’s Blood. The chicken-wing division has become the league’s tightest four-way contest.

PITTSY’S BOOK

For two weeks, the waterfall had kept running. Pittsy’s Book had not.

The shutters stood closed beneath the temple stone. Green lamps burned above ledgers that offered no new answers. The counters where the Commonwealth once gathered to argue over lines and liabilities had fallen into an uncomfortable silence.

The League’s records examiner came looking for a crime.
What he found was an absence.

No confirmed missing fortune. No proven conspiracy. Not even a respectable ransom demand. Just the Book’s closed windows, unanswered questions, and a proprietor whose three heads had apparently found something more interesting than taking wagers.

Three Dreaded Snake had survived The LLC by thirty-seven hundredths of a point. The result was official. The Book remained closed.

The examiner turned the final page of his notes.

pages.title: Final Word
pages.text:
SCHEMIN ’26 | WEEK 6 RECAP | FOLIO 24
FINAL WORD
THE COMMONWEALTH KEEPS MOVING.

There are two ways to judge a week in the Commonwealth. One is to ask who won. The other is to look at what the winners left behind.

At the ruins, a visiting song that would not stop. At the country club, a toast delivered with the windows shut against the rain. At Foothill Camp, chalk lines nobody trusted. At the Chili Stable, a missing meal that might yet become an institution. In the swamp, a deed without title. At the waterfall, a bridge without a bridge.

The scores are final for now; the arguments are not.
Next week, Red Leopards welcomes His Majesty’s Blood in the officially chosen Game of the Week. The house is already preparing for company. Whether the guest enjoys the welcome remains a story for another edition.
